attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I've poured months of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b07/review-experiment-blkzujvr/call-8ff05569bcf44fcb93a3019a355b894a/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs');p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 text=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 (p/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+(p/f'page-{i+1:02d}.txt').read_text() for i in range(len(r.pages))))
print((p/'page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for i in range(1,12):
 for ext in ('txt','png'):
  (p/f'page-{i:02d}.{ext}').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(p/'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
if p.exists() and not any(p.iterdir()):
 p.rmdir()
print('Review complete; temporary extraction and rendering files removed.')
PY"

strengths: The paper identifies a useful limitation of agent-count curricula: adding agents can simplify some cooperative tasks while complicating others. The contrast between coverage and XOR tasks clearly motivates adapting the curriculum direction.

Combining self-paced task selection with MAPPO and critic-loss prioritization is a practical, potentially useful contribution. Parameter sharing and observation padding address transfer across agent counts, and the direct SPRL baseline helps assess the proposed objective change.

Experiments cover three distinct cooperative settings and separately show target-task performance, training performance, and generated curricula. They provide encouraging evidence that adaptive agent-count curricula overcome exploration failures of direct MAPPO. SPMARL shows earlier learning particularly on Simple-Spread, whose results include five seeds and 95% confidence intervals.
weaknesses: The central interpretation of critic loss as learning progress is insufficiently supported. Equation 8 measures return prediction error, which combines critic approximation error with return variability. It can remain high under an unchanged policy or decrease through critic fitting alone. Access to the full state does not eliminate these effects. The paper provides no direct measurements linking this score to subsequent policy improvement or reduced credit-assignment difficulty, so the proposed explanation for the gains remains speculative.

The optimization is mathematically problematic as written. Equation 6 minimizes KL(p || µ), while µ is described as a Dirac target and p as a Gaussian curriculum. This divergence is infinite whenever the curriculum assigns probability outside the target. A nondegenerate target approximation or another well-defined objective must be specified. The treatment of discretization and clipping in the importance weights also needs clarification.

The comparisons provide limited evidence against existing curriculum methods. DyMA-CL, EPC, and VACL are represented by a generic linear schedule, which omits their other mechanisms. In Simple-Spread, the increasing linear schedule is explicitly acknowledged to make exploration harder, but a decreasing schedule or a tuned easy-task warm-start baseline is absent. These choices weaken the claim of superiority over prior multi-agent curriculum approaches.

The originality of critic-loss-based task selection is not adequately situated. Prioritized Level Replay (Jiang et al., 2021), for example, already uses value-error-based signals to prioritize environments with estimated learning potential and is not discussed. The multi-agent adaptation may still be valuable, but the manuscript should distinguish that contribution from the broader idea of using critic errors for curriculum selection.

The evidence for consistently faster convergence is limited. Only one configuration per benchmark and one underlying learner are evaluated; the XOR curves for SPRL and SPMARL nearly overlap, and final performance is generally comparable. Quantified time-to-performance or learning-curve summaries with uncertainty would make the speed claim easier to assess. There are also no controls separating the benefit of using all trajectory states from the choice of critic loss, or sensitivity analyses for the performance threshold and KL bound.

Important reproduction details are omitted or deferred to the linked code, including complete curriculum initialization and bounds, most threshold values, network and optimizer settings, and how changing XOR action spaces are handled. The timing and aggregation of critic-loss measurements are especially important for the proposed mechanism. Algorithm 1 also appears to resume stage-one optimization when performance falls below the threshold, whereas Section 4.1 describes freezing the distribution after entering stage two. Separately, the SMAC discussion’s reference to an eight-agent target conflicts with the five-agent target elsewhere and should be corrected.
